title: Call: Lindgren 4th Floor — ULT-L4-09 Box Count Short

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EHS Biosafety Office ext. 5-0142 (speakerphone)

caller.name: Raj
caller.label: Lab manager, Lindgren Life Sciences 4th floor (ULT-L4-09 user)

callee.name: Biosafety Officer
callee.label: EHS Biosafety Office, on speaker in the incident room

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: Hi, this is Raj, lab manager on four. Sorry, I know you've got a lot going on downstairs. We did our quarterly box count on ULT-L4-09 this morning.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: The EHS portal inventory lists two hundred twelve vials in rack C. We count one ninety-eight. That's fourteen short, and they're all in two boxes. The labels on one of those boxes are handwritten, and they don't match the portal record numbers.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: And with the sensor dropping out on four earlier... I don't know. It feels like a lot for one morning.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: One of our postdocs is saying that if anything in there were regulated, we'd owe a select agent report and a Form 3 within the hour. He wants to call CDC himself. He's got the number up on his screen right now.

transcript.speaker: Faculty member (incident room)
transcript.text: If vials are missing on the same morning as a spill, we should report first and sort it out later. That's the safe call.

transcript.speaker: Raj
transcript.text: So... do we stop using the freezer? Do I call someone? Do I tell him not to call? I need to tell him something in the next few minutes, because he's not going to wait long.

voiceStyles.Raj: Man in his 30s, polite but rattled, speaking fast, a lab office with a freezer compressor humming behind him
voiceStyles.Faculty member (incident room): Senior faculty voice in the room, firm and confident, speaking over the speakerphone

instructorNote: This is a red herring. Players should treat the mismatch as a records question, not a loss. The BSO should start a search (transfer log, unsigned destruction entries, box labels, portal edit history) and tell the lab not to call any agency. The IO should restate that HSU holds no select agents. The IBC chair should open this as a separate file from LI-2026-0142, to be classified only after the search. Watch whether the faculty member's "report first" pressure, or the mix-up between ULT-L4-17 and ULT-L4-09, pushes anyone into a Federal Select Agent Program call.
